llm.summary: The skill's code, docs, and dependencies are consistent with its stated purpose (converting Markdown to PNGs); it does not request credentials or external endpoints, though it writes files and runs a headless browser which have expected resource and privacy implications.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included code and dependencies: marked + Puppeteer are appropriate for rendering Markdown to images. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions confine themselves to reading Markdown, rendering to HTML, running Puppeteer, writing PNG(s) and logs, and returning image paths. Caveats: the skill writes temporary files and per-image .log files (which may contain input text or error stacks), and SKILL.md suggests writing to /tmp and embedding file paths in messages — this has privacy implications but is consistent with the stated functionality.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec in registry (instruction-only), but package.json/package-lock are included and declare Puppeteer and marked. Running this will require npm install; Puppeteer typically downloads a Chromium binary at install/runtime which increases disk/network activity. There is no download-from-untrusted-URL pattern in the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables, credentials, or external config paths. No sensitive system access is requested beyond normal filesystem writes needed to produce images.

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it claims (convert Markdown to PNG) and does not request credentials or contact external endpoints. Before installing, consider: 

- Puppeteer will require npm install and typically downloads a Chromium binary (~100+ MB); be prepared for disk and network usage.
- The code launches Chromium with --no-sandbox, which is common in containerized environments but reduces process isolation; run in a sandboxed environment if possible.
- The skill writes output PNGs and .log files (which may include original content and error stacks) to disk — these can contain sensitive text; configure and monitor the output directory and enable the described whitelist/cleanup options.
- Review package-lock.json if you need supply-chain assurance and ensure you trust the npm packages; consider installing dependencies in an isolated environment and pinning known-good versions.
- The skill embeds local file paths into messages (e.g., <qqimg>...</qqimg>); ensure your message-sending environment only exposes files to intended recipients.

If you need stronger assurance, run the script in an isolated VM/container, inspect installed node_modules, and verify that logs do not leak sensitive content before using in production.
